Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of ISS vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which intermittent serum starvation may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
The provided dataset (“ijms-24-14743-v2_crc_cells_serum_starv_vs_dmso_DEG.csv”) reports differential expression (log2FC, padj) for 20,130 genes in colorectal cancer cells treated with intermittent serum starvation (ISS) versus DMSO control. 6555 genes reach padj < 0.05; both up- and down-regulated genes were combined for Reactome over-representation analysis.  Details on cell line, replicate number, and assay platform are not specified.  

Key Reactome pathways (combined up/down DE genes)  
Reactome ORA (Fisher’s exact test; padj < 0.05) on all significant DE genes (n = 6555) highlights lipid metabolic reprogramming, unfolded protein response, cell-cycle control, peroxisomal function, and membrane trafficking. Below are selected top terms with their DE gene overlaps.

1. Cholesterol Biosynthesis (Reactome_Pathways_2024)  
   • Adjusted P-value: 1.37 × 10⁻⁶  
   • Overlap: 23/27 genes  
   • DE Genes: IDI1; FDPS; SREBF1; MVK; HMGCS1; CYP51A1; MSMO1; DHCR24; HMGCR; HSD17B7; LSS; ACAT2; SREBF2; TM7SF2; SQLE; EBP; NSDHL; PMVK; SC5D; MVD; DHCR7; LBR; FDFT1  
   • Direction: nearly all are up-regulated in ISS (e.g., HMGCR log2FC ≈ +0.09 padj < 0.05; SREBF1 log2FC ≈ + 0.10 padj < 0.05).  

2. Regulation of Cholesterol Biosynthesis by SREBP (SREBF)  
   • Adjusted P-value: 6.7 × 10⁻⁹  
   • Overlap: 42/56 genes (subset shown above)  
   • DE Genes: includes SREBF1, SREBF2, HMGCR, MVK, FDPS, MBTPS1/2, INSIG1/2, SCAP  

3. ATF6 (ATF6-alpha) Activates Chaperones  
   • Adjusted P-value: 6.46 × 10⁻³  
   • Overlap: 10/12 genes  
   • DE Genes: MBTPS1; XBP1; HSPA5; NFYA; NFYB; DDIT3; CALR; ATF6; MBTPS2; HSP90B1  
   • Direction: predominantly down-regulated (e.g., XBP1 log2FC ≈ –0.10 padj < 0.05; HSPA5 log2FC ≈ –0.04 padj < 0.05).  

4. Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) / IRE1-alpha Activates Chaperones  
   • Adjusted P-value: 4.24 × 10⁻⁸  
   • Overlap: 41/95 genes  
   • DE Genes: CUL7; SHC1; GOSR2; CXXC1; DNAJB9; SSR1; EXTL3; SEC31A; ZBTB17; XBP1; HSPA5; …; ATF6  

5. TP53-Mediated Cell-Cycle Regulation  
   a) “TP53 Regulates Transcription of Additional Cell Cycle Genes With Uncertain Roles” (Adj p = 1.93 × 10⁻⁴; Genes: PLK3; BTG2; PLK2; CDC25C; CNOT family; TP53)  
   b) “TP53 Regulates Transcription of Genes Involved in G2 Cell Cycle Arrest” (Adj p = 1.91 × 10⁻³; Genes: PCNA; GADD45A; CDC25C; BAX; SFN; TP53; etc.)  

6. TYSND1 Cleaves Peroxisomal Proteins  
   • Adjusted P-value: 6.34 × 10⁻³  
   • Overlap: 7/7 genes (PHYH; SCP2; ACOX1; AGPS; HSD17B4; TYSND1; ACAA1)  
   • Direction: mixed; ACOX1 and SCP2 are down, whereas TYSND1 is up.  

Discussion  
Intermittent serum starvation in CRC cells induces a coordinated up-regulation of de novo cholesterol synthesis (SREBF-HMGCR axis; FDPS, MVK, SQLE), likely to support membrane remodeling under nutrient stress. Concomitant activation of SREBP regulatory machinery (MBTPS1/2, SCAP, INSIG1/2) suggests enhanced SREBP proteolytic maturation. Conversely, key UPR effectors (XBP1, HSPA5, ATF6) are down-regulated, implying ISS may attenuate ER-stress signaling or shift balance toward pro-apoptotic arms (up-regulation of DDIT3). p53-driven cell-cycle checkpoints (CDC25C, PCNA, CCNB1, GADD45A, BAX) are significantly over-represented, indicating growth arrest/G2-M blockade. Peroxisomal protein processing (TYSND1, ACOX1, SCP2) and fatty acid metabolism (ELOVL5, FADS2) are also enriched, pointing to lipid catabolism remodeling. Membrane trafficking and ER–Golgi transport terms reflect broad alterations in secretory pathway, potentially to reprogram receptor recycling under stress.  

Mechanistic Implications  
ISS appears to rewire lipid metabolism—boosting sterol biosynthesis while curtailing ER chaperone capacity—to enforce cell-cycle arrest via p53 and shift redox/vacuolar homeostasis through peroxisomes and UPR modulation. This dual metabolic–stress response axis may underlie ISS-mediated inhibition of CRC proliferation and sensitize cells to therapy.
